title: Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer partners with Legora to empower lawyers with advanced AI tools
author: Legora

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: HSF Kramer’s announcement supports the platform-led adoption narrative through firmwide deployment, integration with its existing technology stack, a phased client portal and investment in lawyer upskilling. It also reinforces the synthesis’s evidentiary caution: the source reports intended capabilities and client benefits, not measured productivity, accuracy or outcomes.
qs: We are investing in leading legal technology and upskilling our people in using it to the highest standards.

kp.k: Firmwide AI adoption targets everyday legal tasks
kp.d: The March 12, 2026 Legora press release announces Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer's adoption of Legora as its firmwide general-purpose AI platform. It describes lawyer support across drafting, document interaction, insights generation, data analysis, summarisation and translation. Better client outcomes are an asserted benefit, rather than a measured finding reported in the release.
qs: Leading global law firm Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer is adopting Legora as its firmwide general-purpose AI platform, marking a significant step in the firm’s investment in innovation and technology‑enabled legal services.
Legora will act as an “intelligent legal colleague”.
It supports smarter drafting and interaction with documents, insights generation, data analysis, summarisation and translation, enabling our lawyers to deliver even better outcomes for clients.

kp.k: Client portal extends AI into collaborative service delivery
kp.d: The announced phased rollout includes a client portal intended to enable more direct client engagement, secure collaboration and file sharing. These are planned changes to the client delivery interface; the release does not report completed rollout results.
qs: As part of the phased rollout, HSF Kramer will also adopt Legora’s client portal to facilitate more direct client engagement through the platform – supporting secure collaboration, streamlined file sharing, a data-enriched document experience, and an AI-powered client delivery.

kp.k: Firm leadership links competitive differentiation to technology and upskilling
kp.d: In a customer quotation carried by Legora, Global CEO Justin D’Agostino predicts that sophisticated technology combined with highly trained lawyers will differentiate leading global firms. He describes investment in legal technology and staff upskilling, placing this announcement within more than 15 years of legal technology activity and referencing the previous year's Chief AI Officer appointment.
qs: The combination of sophisticated technology with highly-trained lawyers will define – and differentiate – the world’s leading global law firms.
We are investing in leading legal technology and upskilling our people in using it to the highest standards.

This is another milestone in more than 15 years of pioneering and embracing legal tech, including our established global Digital Legal Delivery practice and of course last year's hire of Ilona Logvinova as our Chief AI Officer.

kp.k: Chief AI Officer frames adoption as strategic partnership
kp.d: Chief AI Officer Ilona Logvinova describes Legora as part of the firm's wider technology stack and global client-support strategy. She frames the relationship as an opportunity to shape AI-enabled legal delivery, rather than solely acquire software; these are the customer's strategic intentions quoted in the vendor release.
qs: Legora is key to our AI strategy – delivering the depth, user experience, and collaborative capabilities we need to support clients globally.
Bringing Legora into our firm enhances our wider tech stack and advances our firm’s ambitions by strengthening innovative delivery to our clients.
We see this as a strategic partnership and an opportunity to continue to shape cutting‑edge AI in legal delivery, for the benefit of our clients.

kp.k: Digital delivery practice combines legal and operational expertise
kp.d: The release describes an existing Digital Legal Delivery practice operating across every firm region and combining legal experts, technologists, legal operations professionals and project managers. It attributes support for clients' digital evolution and development of new digital services to this multidisciplinary team.
qs: HSF Kramer has a dedicated Digital Legal Delivery practice – which operates across every region of our firm – brings together legal experts, technologists, legal operations professionals and project managers — this multidisciplinary team supports clients with their digital evolution, and enables the development of new and innovative digital services that respond to the rapidly evolving business landscape.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: The press release presents Legora as a firmwide tool that augments lawyers’ work and improves client outcomes.
pts.d: The Legora newsroom release announces HSF Kramer’s adoption of Legora as its general-purpose AI platform. It claims support for drafting, document interaction, insight generation, data analysis, summarisation and translation will enable lawyers to deliver better client outcomes. The framing is assistance to lawyers through an 'intelligent legal colleague', rather than replacement of lawyers or autonomous legal delivery.

pts.k: The release claims a client portal will enable more direct client engagement and AI-supported collaboration and delivery.
pts.d: The planned portal adoption extends AI use beyond internal lawyer workflows to the firm–client relationship. The release identifies secure collaboration, streamlined file sharing and a data-enriched document experience as intended functions and benefits.

pts.k: Justin D’Agostino predicts that sophisticated technology combined with highly trained lawyers will differentiate leading global law firms.
pts.d: HSF Kramer’s Global CEO links future competitive differentiation to a combination of technology investment and lawyer capability. His statement presents upskilling as part of the firm’s response, rather than suggesting that acquiring software alone produces differentiation.

pts.k: Ilona Logvinova claims the partnership strengthens global client delivery; Max Junestrand claims the adoption approach enhances legal work while maintaining quality and trust.
pts.d: HSF Kramer’s Chief AI Officer, Ilona Logvinova, describes Legora’s depth, user experience and collaborative capabilities as supporting clients globally and the partnership as an opportunity to shape AI-enabled legal delivery. Legora CEO and co-founder Max Junestrand presents HSF Kramer’s approach as an example of how leading global firms can enhance legal work without sacrificing quality and trust. These are attributed strategic and benefit claims, not reported performance results.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The release relies on the adoption announcement, executive assertions and the firm’s technology experience; it provides no measured results for the claimed benefits.
pts.d: The concrete organisational example is HSF Kramer’s announced adoption and planned portal rollout. Supporting context includes D’Agostino’s account of more than 15 years of legal-technology activity, the appointment of a Chief AI Officer and an established multidisciplinary Digital Legal Delivery practice. Claims about better outcomes, enhanced work, differentiation, quality and trust are supported by statements from firm and vendor leaders, not by supplied benchmarks, client case results, quantitative data or independent evaluations.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Adoption is underway as of March 12, 2026, with a phased rollout; benefits and competitive differentiation are forward-looking without a completion date.
pts.d: The publication date anchors the announcement. The platform is described as being adopted, while the portal is a future component of the phased rollout. No rollout completion date or quantified benefit horizon is supplied. D’Agostino’s differentiation prediction is conditioned on combining sophisticated technology with highly trained lawyers, supported by investment and upskilling. Logvinova frames further development of legal AI as an ongoing partnership opportunity.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The identified beneficiaries are HSF Kramer’s lawyers and global clients, with broader implications asserted for leading global law firms.
pts.d: Lawyers are to receive AI assistance across document and analytical tasks and training in technology use. Clients are promised better outcomes, stronger digital delivery and more direct platform-based engagement. Leading global firms are the segment addressed by the competitive-differentiation prediction. The release situates implementation within a multidisciplinary practice involving legal experts, technologists, legal operations professionals and project managers, but does not predict changes to their headcount or staffing structure. It makes no specific claims about fees, entry-level displacement or access to justice.
